title: Notifications and permission UX (overview)
learningObjectives: Explain notifications and permission ux (overview) and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: The Notifications API can display system notifications when supported and permitted. Permission should be requested in response to a clear user gesture after explaining the benefit. Persistent notifications are commonly coordinated with a service worker; support and behaviour vary by browser and platform.
understand.whyItMatters: Notifications can interrupt users and expose information on a lock screen. Use them sparingly, request permission contextually, and avoid sending sensitive content.
understand.analogy: A notification is an interruption delivered outside the page; it should be invited and genuinely useful.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The permission request follows a click. The notification is shown only when permission is granted and the API is supported.

examples.code: document.querySelector('#notify')?.addEventListener('click',async()=>{if(!('Notification'in window))return console.log('Not supported');const permission=await Notification.requestPermission();if(permission==='granted')new Notification('CodeSaathi',{body:'Your lesson is ready.'})});
examples.explanation: The permission request follows a click. The notification is shown only when permission is granted and the API is supported.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Add an opt-in notification control with a clear explanation, denial fallback, and a setting to disable future notices.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: When is it appropriate to request notification permission?
options: After explaining the benefit and following a user gesture
questions.answer: After explaining the benefit and following a user gesture
questions.explanation: Permission should be requested contextually after the user understands the benefit.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
